function getParameterByName(name, url) {
		if(url == null){
		  url = window.location.href;
		}
	    name = name.replace(/[\[\]]/g, '\\$&');
	    var regex = new RegExp('[?&]' + name + '(=([^&#]*)|&|#|$)'),
		results = regex.exec(url);
	    if (!results) return null;
	    if (!results[2]) return '';
	    return decodeURIComponent(results[2].replace(/\+/g, ' '));
	}

    var STYLE_ID = 'at-body-style';

    return doc.getElementsByTagName('head')[0];
    }
    function addStyle(parent, id, def) {
        if (!parent) {
        return;
        }
        var style = doc.createElement('style');
        style.id = id;
        style.innerHTML = def;
        parent.appendChild(style);
    }
    function removeStyle(parent, id) {
        if (!parent) {
            return;
        }
        var style = doc.getElementById(id);
        if (!style) {
            return;
        }
        parent.removeChild(style);
    }
    addStyle(getParent(), STYLE_ID, style);
    setTimeout(function() {
    removeStyle(getParent(), STYLE_ID);

 * @license MIT

	String.prototype.replaceAll = function(str, newStr){
		// If a regex pattern
		if (Object.prototype.toString.call(str).toLowerCase() === '[object regexp]') {
			return this.replace(str, newStr);
		}
		// If a string
		return this.replace(new RegExp(str, 'g'), newStr);

	function getCookie(cname) {
	 	var name = cname + "=";
  		var decodedCookie = decodeURIComponent(document.cookie);
		var ca = decodedCookie.split(';');
  		for(var i = 0; i <ca.length; i++) {
    			var c = ca[i];
    			while (c.charAt(0) == ' ') {
     				 c = c.substring(1);
    			}
    			if (c.indexOf(name) == 0) {
    				 return c.substring(name.length, c.length);
    			}
  		}
  		return "";
	}

	var referer = "";//sessionStorage.container;

function callMainSitePrismaNavHTML(){

    sessionStorage.setItem("domain",referrer_domain);

        }

        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/cortexsearch";	
    }

        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=sase&domain=en';
        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/sasesearch";

function addStyle(styles) {            
    /* Create style document */
    var css = document.createElement('style');
    css.type = 'text/css';

    if (css.styleSheet) 
        css.styleSheet.cssText = styles;
    else 
        css.appendChild(document.createTextNode(styles));

    /* Append style to the tag name */
    document.getElementsByTagName("head")[0].appendChild(css);
}
function httpGet(theUrl,req_type) {
    if (window.XMLHttpRequest) { // code for IE7+, Firefox, Chrome, Opera, Safari
        xmlhttp=new XMLHttpRequest();
    } else {// code for IE6, IE5
        xmlhttp=new ActiveXObject("Microsoft.XMLHTTP");
    }
    xmlhttp.onreadystatechange=function()
    {
        if (xmlhttp.readyState==4 && xmlhttp.status==200)
        {
            if(req_type == 'menu_html'){
            var nav_text = xmlhttp.responseText.replaceAll('https://static.cloud.coveo.com/searchui/v2.9159/js/CoveoJsSearch.Lazy.min.js', '');
            nav_text = nav_text.replaceAll('src="/', 'src="'+maindomain_lang+'/');
            nav_text = nav_text.replaceAll("src='/", "src='"+maindomain_lang+"/");
            nav_text = nav_text.replaceAll("'/content", "'"+maindomain_lang+"/content");
                        
            document.getElementById("PAN_2021_NAV_ASYNC").innerHTML = nav_text.replaceAll('href="/', 'href="'+maindomain_lang+'/');

            var lozad_back = document.getElementsByClassName('lozad-background');
            Array.prototype.forEach.call(lozad_back, function(el) {
            // Do stuff here
            var el_back_img_path = el.getAttribute('data-background-image');
            var first_pos = el_back_img_path.indexOf("'");
            var last_pos = el_back_img_path.indexOf("'",first_pos+1);
            el_back_img_path = el_back_img_path.substring(first_pos+1,last_pos);
            let result = el_back_img_path.includes(main_site_url);
            if(result == false){
                el.setAttribute("data-background-image",main_site_url+el_back_img_path);
            }
            else{
                el.setAttribute("data-background-image",el_back_img_path);
            }
            });
            const observer_lozad = lozad('.lozad, .lozad-background'); // lazy loads elements with default selector as '.lozad'
            observer_lozad.observe();
            }
            if(req_type == 'head_inline_css'){
            addStyle(xmlhttp.responseText);
            }
        }
    }
    xmlhttp.open("GET", theUrl, true );
    xmlhttp.send();    
}    
    
if(referer == 'Prisma' || referer == 'CloudCortex' || referer == 'Cortex' || referer == 'Sase' || referer == 'Unit' || referer == 'Ngfw' || referer == 'Idira'){

    else if(referer == 'Ngfw'){
        article.dataset.type = 'ngfw';

        $('#PAN_2021_NAV_ASYNC').removeClass('default').addClass('defaultRedesigned');

    <section class="section blog-contents">

            <div class="be__contents">
              <div class="be__contents-wrapper">
                <h2><a id="post-182510-_4lt92rr5muov"></a>Executive Summary</h2>
<p>We discovered a vulnerability in the Google Cloud Vertex AI software development kit (SDK) for Python, and responsibly disclosed it to Google. Before Google’s fix, the vulnerability would have allowed an attacker operating entirely from their own Google Cloud project to hijack a victim's model upload and poison it. By exploiting this flaw in vulnerable versions of the SDK, an attacker can achieve remote code execution (RCE) within a target’s Vertex AI serving infrastructure, with zero initial access to the victim's project.</p>
<p>The root enabler of this attack is a predictable default bucket name, combined with a missing ownership check in the SDK's staging logic. When a Vertex AI user uploads a model without specifying a custom staging bucket, the SDK constructs a bucket name using a deterministic pattern based on the project ID and region.</p>
<p>An attacker who knows the victim's project ID can preemptively create this bucket in their own project, a technique known as bucket squatting. The SDK then silently uploads the victim's model artifacts to the attacker-controlled bucket. Subsequently, within a narrow window of opportunity, the attacker replaces the legitimate model with one that carries a malicious payload. Once the victim deploys the compromised model, the attacker's code executes. In vulnerable SDK versions, this can lead to data exfiltration, lateral movement and further compromise of the victim's cloud environment.</p>
<p>We refer to the process of exploiting this vulnerability as Pickle in the Middle because it relies in part on deserializing a built-in module called <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle</span>, as explained below in Pickle Deserialization as Attack Vector.</p>
<p>We reported the vulnerability to the Google security team, and they accepted our findings. The issue affected <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">google-cloud-aiplatform</span> SDK versions 1.139.0 and 1.140.0, which was the latest at the time of testing. Google completed the fixes to address this issue in v1.148.0, which was released April 15, 2026.</p>
<p>We recommend that developers upgrade to fixed versions of the SDK.</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/r/Cortex-CLOUD/Cortex-Cloud-Runtime-Security-Documentation/What-is-Cortex-Cloud" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Cortex Cloud</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/cortex/cloud/ai-security-posture-management" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Cortex AI-SPM</a></li>
</ul>
<p>The <a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/unit42/assess/ai-security-assessment" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Unit 42 AI Security Assessment</a> and <a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/unit42/ai-advantage" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Unit 42 Frontier AI Defense</a> service can help identify and mitigate complex AI-specific risks.</p>
<p>If you think you might have been compromised or have an urgent matter, contact the <a href="https://start.paloaltonetworks.com/contact-unit42.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Unit 42 Incident Response team</a>.</p>

<h2><a id="post-182510-_htizzce9xl76"></a>Background and Terminology</h2>
<p><a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Vertex AI</a> is a machine learning platform for training and deploying ML models and AI applications. The Vertex AI SDK for Python is the primary client library that developers use to interact with the platform programmatically. We focused our research on the Vertex AI SDK for Python (<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">google-cloud-aiplatform</span>), as many enterprises rely on it to create and manage their AI/ML pipelines, applications and models.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/model-registry/introduction" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Vertex AI Model Registry</a> is a centralized repository within Vertex AI where users store, version and manage their ML models. When a user uploads a model to the Model Registry via the SDK, the SDK first stages the model artifacts in a Google Cloud Service (GCS) bucket before registering them with the service. The Model Registry then references these staged artifacts. When the model is deployed to an endpoint, Google's internal infrastructure (specifically, a Per-Product, Per-Project Service Account or P4SA) loads them into a serving container. Figure 1 shows the intended model upload flow.</p>
<figure id="attachment_182511" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-182511" style="width: 800px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-182511 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-655014-182510-1.png" alt="A diagram illustrating the Model Registry upload flow. The &quot;User Project&quot; section shows &quot;Model.upload()&quot; leading to &quot;Staging Bucket,&quot; which connects to &quot;Model Registry.&quot; The &quot;Tenant Project&quot; section shows &quot;Google Vertex AI Service Agent&quot; reading from and pushing to &quot;Model Registry,&quot; and deploying to &quot;Model Deployed.&quot; Arrows depict the direction of data flow between the components." width="800" height="601" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-655014-182510-1.png 972w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-655014-182510-1-586x440.png 586w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-655014-182510-1-932x700.png 932w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-655014-182510-1-768x577.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 800px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-182511" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 1. Uploading a model to Model Registry.</figcaption></figure>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_626p2ls2gfxs"></a>Bucket Squatting</h3>
<p>Bucket squatting is a class of vulnerability that takes advantage of the global uniqueness of cloud storage bucket names. Since no two buckets across all of Google Cloud can share the same name, an attacker who is able to predict a bucket name can preemptively create it in their own project. Any subsequent attempt to use a bucket with that name, even from a different project, silently falls back to the attacker's bucket.</p>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_33fsganv0p1v"></a>Service Agents and Tenant Project</h3>
<p>In Google Cloud, many managed services operate through service agents (P4SAs). These are Google-managed service accounts that allow Google Cloud services to access resources. In the case of Vertex AI, the P4SA is responsible for reading model artifacts from the staging bucket and loading them into the serving infrastructure.</p>
<p><a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-infrastructure/docs/glossary#tenant" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Tenant projects</a> are Google Cloud projects that are owned by Google and used to host resources of a managed service. The identities and resources available inside these tenant projects are important aspects to research because they bridge the boundary between Google's infrastructure and the customer's resources. Vertex AI uses tenant projects to host resources such as Kubernetes clusters, containers and service accounts that allow the service to function.</p>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_vaznvyz34vz6"></a>Pickle Deserialization as Attack Vector</h3>
<p><a href="https://joblib.readthedocs.io/en/stable/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Joblib</a> is a set of tools that provides lightweight pipelining in Python. <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle</span></a> is a built-in module used for serializing and deserializing object structures. ML models in the Python ecosystem are commonly serialized using <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle</span> – or its Joblib wrapper. A critical property of <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle</span> is that deserialization can be leveraged to execute code. Specifically, Python's <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle</span> <span style="font-family: georgia, palatino, serif;">protocol</span> supports a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">__reduce__</span> method that defines how an object should be reconstructed. An attacker who controls a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle</span> file can define a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">__reduce__</span> method that executes arbitrary Python code the moment <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">joblib.load()</span> or <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle.load()</span> is called, before any type of validation occurs. This is a well-known property of <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle</span> (and <a href="https://joblib.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/joblib.load.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">joblib</a>), and it is the mechanism we used to turn model poisoning into remote code execution.</p>
<h2><a id="post-182510-_azlx9tkuu4en"></a>The Vulnerability</h2>
<p>The Vertex AI SDK for Python model upload functionality is vulnerable to bucket squatting in versions 1.139.0 and 1.140.0, the latest versions that were available at the time of testing. When a user does not explicitly provide a staging bucket name, the SDK constructs a bucket name deterministically from the project ID and region, and then checks whether the bucket exists. If the bucket does not exist, the SDK creates it. However, if the bucket exists, the SDK does not verify whether the bucket belongs to the caller's project. This means that an attacker can create a bucket with the same name in their own project, and then wait for the victim to upload a model. Once uploaded, the attacker can replace it with a malicious model. This model carries a payload that executes arbitrary code when deployed and loaded, abusing the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pickle</span> deserialization mechanism.</p>
<h2><a id="post-182510-_yq9yivl4x1ju"></a>Discovery Methodology</h2>
<p>As part of this research, we incorporated a large language model (LLM) into the discovery and code-analysis phase. Analysis that once took days can now be executed significantly faster. By iteratively narrowing the model's focus and instructing it to look for specific patterns, we found paths that led to resources provisioned on the cloud, affected by user-controlled or project-derived inputs.</p>
<p>The vulnerable code was located in <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">gcs_utils.py</span>, inside the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">stage_local_data_in_gcs()</span> function:</p><!-- Crayon Syntax Highlighter v_2.7.2_beta -->

		<div id="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340" class="crayon-syntax crayon-theme-classic crayon-font-monaco crayon-os-pc print-yes notranslate" data-settings=" minimize scroll-mouseover wrap" style=" margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 12px; font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important;">
		
			<div class="crayon-toolbar" data-settings=" mouseover overlay hide delay" style="font-size: 12px !important;height: 18px !important; line-height: 18px !important;"><span class="crayon-title"></span>
			<div class="crayon-tools" style="font-size: 12px !important;height: 18px !important; line-height: 18px !important;"><div class="crayon-button crayon-nums-button" title="Toggle Line Numbers"><div class="crayon-button-icon"></div></div><div class="crayon-button crayon-plain-button" title="Toggle Plain Code"><div class="crayon-button-icon"></div></div><div class="crayon-button crayon-wrap-button" title="Toggle Line Wrap"><div class="crayon-button-icon"></div></div><div class="crayon-button crayon-expand-button" title="Expand Code"><div class="crayon-button-icon"></div></div><div class="crayon-button crayon-copy-button" title="Copy"><div class="crayon-button-icon"></div></div><div class="crayon-button crayon-popup-button" title="Open Code In New Window"><div class="crayon-button-icon"></div></div></div></div>
			<div class="crayon-info" style="min-height: 16.8px !important; line-height: 16.8px !important;"></div>
			<div class="crayon-plain-wrap"><textarea  class="crayon-plain print-no" data-settings="dblclick" readonly style="-moz-tab-size:4; -o-tab-size:4; -webkit-tab-size:4; tab-size:4; font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important;">
staging_bucket_name = project + "-vertex-staging-" + location # ← Deterministic predictable name
client = storage.Client(project=project, credentials=credentials)
staging_bucket = storage.Bucket(client=client, name=staging_bucket_name)
if not staging_bucket.exists():       # ← Only checks existence, NOT ownership
    staging_bucket = client.create_bucket(...)
staging_gcs_dir = "gs://" + staging_bucket_name</textarea></div>

					<div class="crayon-nums-content" style="font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important;"><div class="crayon-num" data-line="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-1">1</div><div class="crayon-num crayon-striped-num" data-line="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-2">2</div><div class="crayon-num" data-line="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-3">3</div><div class="crayon-num crayon-striped-num" data-line="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-4">4</div><div class="crayon-num" data-line="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-5">5</div><div class="crayon-num crayon-striped-num" data-line="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-6">6</div></div>
				</td>
						<td class="crayon-code"><div class="crayon-pre" style="font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important; -moz-tab-size:4; -o-tab-size:4; -webkit-tab-size:4; tab-size:4;"><div class="crayon-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-1"><span class="crayon-i">staging_bucket_name</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>=<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">project</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>+<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-s">"-vertex-staging-"</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>+<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">location</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-p"># ← Deterministic predictable name</span></div><div class="crayon-line crayon-striped-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-2"><span class="crayon-i">client</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>=<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">storage</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-e">Client</span><span class="crayon-sy">(</span><span class="crayon-i">project</span>=<span class="crayon-i">project</span><span class="crayon-sy">,</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">credentials</span>=<span class="crayon-i">credentials</span><span class="crayon-sy">)</span></div><div class="crayon-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-3"><span class="crayon-i">staging_bucket</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>=<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">storage</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-e">Bucket</span><span class="crayon-sy">(</span><span class="crayon-i">client</span>=<span class="crayon-i">client</span><span class="crayon-sy">,</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">name</span>=<span class="crayon-i">staging_bucket_name</span><span class="crayon-sy">)</span></div><div class="crayon-line crayon-striped-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-4"><span class="crayon-st">if</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-st">not</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">staging_bucket</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-e">exists</span><span class="crayon-sy">(</span><span class="crayon-sy">)</span><span class="crayon-sy">:</span><span class="crayon-h">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span><span class="crayon-p"># ← Only checks existence, NOT ownership</span></div><div class="crayon-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-5"><span class="crayon-h">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</span><span class="crayon-i">staging_bucket</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>=<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">client</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-e">create_bucket</span><span class="crayon-sy">(</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-sy">)</span></div><div class="crayon-line crayon-striped-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d48621951340-6"><span class="crayon-i">staging_gcs_dir</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>=<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-s">"gs://"</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>+<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">staging_bucket_name</span></div></div></td>
					</tr>
				</table>
			</div>
		</div>
<!-- [Format Time: 0.0002 seconds] -->
<p>The function constructs the bucket name deterministically from the project ID and region (e.g., <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">my-project-vertex-staging-us-central1</span>). It then calls <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">staging_bucket.exists()</span> to check whether the bucket already exists. The <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">bucket.exists()</span> call returns <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">True</span> for any bucket with that name, regardless of which project owns it.</p>
<p>If the bucket exists, even in a completely different project, the SDK proceeds to upload model artifacts to it without any further verification. Once the model is uploaded, the attacker has a limited window of opportunity to replace it with a compromised one. This malicious model carries a payload that executes arbitrary code when the model is deployed and loaded. After this window, the <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents#ai-platform-service-agent" target="_blank" rel="noopener">AI Platform Service Agent</a> (<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount[.]com</span>) reads the model and the attacker loses their ability to replace it. Our tests show that this window is approximately 2.5 seconds, requiring near-real-time attacker operation, as shown in Phases 2-4 below.</p>
<h2><a id="post-182510-_6q3uuinitruf"></a>The Attack Chain</h2>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_wy0tee9a81lu"></a>Prerequisites</h3>
<p>The success of this attack depends on the following conditions:</p>
<ul>
<li>The victim’s default staging bucket does not already exist in the target region. This is the case for any project that has not yet used Vertex AI in that region or has not used the default staging bucket name.</li>
<li>The victim does not specify an explicit <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">staging_bucket</span> parameter when calling SDK methods like <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">Model.upload()</span>. When no bucket is specified, the SDK falls back to the deterministic default name.</li>
<li>On the attacker's side, the only requirements are a Google Cloud project – in any organization, using any billing account – and knowledge of the victim's project ID, which is often publicly discoverable.</li>
</ul>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_m6s00nqwiygb"></a>High-Level Flow</h3>
<p>The flow of attack phases reflects the key findings of our research:</p>
<ul>
<li>Predictable bucket name and lack of ownership verification, enabling bucket squatting</li>
<li>Race condition window that can be exploited to hijack the model upload</li>
<li>Pickle deserialization as an RCE vector</li>
</ul>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_ho69vt9u90rw"></a>Phase 1: Bucket Squatting</h3>
<p>The attacker preemptively creates a bucket with the predicted name of the target's staging bucket, in the attacker's own project. The attacker then configures identity and access management (IAM) permissions so that any authenticated Google Cloud identity can read from and write to the attacker’s bucket. This is critical, as the victim's identity (that uploads the model) and Vertex AI’s service agent (which reads the model) must both be able to interact with the bucket.</p>
<p>The code snippet below illustrates how any authenticated user could interact with the bucket.</p><!-- Crayon Syntax Highlighter v_2.7.2_beta -->

		<div id="crayon-6a348c6f87d56745003383" class="crayon-syntax crayon-theme-classic crayon-font-monaco crayon-os-pc print-yes notranslate" data-settings=" minimize scroll-mouseover wrap" style=" margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 12px; font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important;">

class="crayon-e">storage </span><span class="crayon-e">buckets </span><span class="crayon-i">add</span>-<span class="crayon-i">iam</span>-<span class="crayon-i">policy</span>-<span class="crayon-i">binding</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-s">"gs://${BUCKET}"</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-sy">\</span></div><div class="crayon-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d56745003383-13"><span class="crayon-h">&nbsp;&nbsp;</span>--<span class="crayon-i">member</span>=<span class="crayon-s">"allAuthenticatedUsers"</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>--<span class="crayon-i">role</span>=<span class="crayon-s">"roles/storage.objectViewer"</span></div></div></td>

				</table>

<!-- [Format Time: 0.0002 seconds] -->
<p>The <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">legacyBucketReader</span> role ensures that when the victim’s SDK checks whether the bucket exists, the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">bucket.exists()</span> returns a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">True</span> response. The <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">objectCreator</span> role allows the victim's SDK to upload artifacts. The <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">objectViewer</span> role allows the Vertex AI service agent to read the artifacts later.</p>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_187y9u5vsg8d"></a>Phase 2: Preparing the Model Replacement Function</h3>
<p>The attacker deploys a Cloud Function, which is a serverless compute service in Google Cloud that executes code in response to events. The function is configured with a trigger on <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">google.storage.object.finalize</span>, which fires every time a new object is created (or overwritten) in the specified bucket. This means that the function automatically executes whenever the victim uploads a model artifact to the squatted bucket.</p>
<p>The attacker-created Cloud Function's logic is straightforward. When it detects a new <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">model.joblib</span> file in a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">vertex_ai_auto_staging</span> path, it downloads the original file and replaces it with a pre-generated malicious payload.</p>
<p>The malicious payload is a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">joblib</span> serialized Python object with a crafted <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">__reduce__</span> method. To check the usage of this method, we set up a webhook that receives the victim's service account credentials. When the model is deserialized, it executes code that queries the Google Compute Engine (GCE) metadata server for the serving container's service account credentials and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled endpoint.</p>
<p>The reason we use a Cloud Function rather than polling the bucket is timing. According to our tests, the window between the victim's upload and the service agent read is approximately 2.5 seconds. A Cloud Function triggered by g<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">oogle.storage.object.finalize</span> reacts within approximately 800 ms, leaving enough time to replace the file before the service agent reads it. In this way, the attacker wins the race. The victim uploads a legitimate model, but by the time the service agent reads it, the file has been swapped.</p>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_m1wigu8kxmxz"></a>Phase 3: Victim Uploads a Model</h3>
<p>The victim runs standard SDK code, without unusual configuration or security mistakes, as shown in the following code block:</p><!-- Crayon Syntax Highlighter v_2.7.2_beta -->

		<div id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5a850741294" class="crayon-syntax crayon-theme-classic crayon-font-monaco crayon-os-pc print-yes notranslate" data-settings=" minimize scroll-mouseover wrap" style=" margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 12px; font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important;">
		
			<div class="crayon-toolbar" data-settings=" mouseover overlay hide delay" style="font-size: 12px !important;height: 18px !important; line-height: 18px !important;"><span class="crayon-title"></span>

aiplatform.init(project="victim-project", location="us-central1")

    display_name="my-model",
    artifact_uri=local_model_dir,
    serving_container_image_uri="us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/prediction/sklearn-cpu.1-0:latest",

					<tr class="crayon-row">

id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5a850741294-3"><span class="crayon-i">vertex_model</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>=<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">aiplatform</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-i">Model</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-e">upload</span><span class="crayon-sy">(</span></div><div class="crayon-line crayon-striped-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5a850741294-4"><span class="crayon-h">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</span><span class="crayon-i">display_name</span>=<span class="crayon-s">"my-model"</span><span class="crayon-sy">,</span></div><div class="crayon-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5a850741294-5"><span class="crayon-h">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</span><span class="crayon-i">artifact_uri</span>=<span class="crayon-i">local_model_dir</span><span class="crayon-sy">,</span></div><div class="crayon-line crayon-striped-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5a850741294-6"><span class="crayon-h">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</span><span class="crayon-i">serving_container_image_uri</span>=<span class="crayon-s">"us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/prediction/sklearn-cpu.1-0:latest"</span><span class="crayon-sy">,</span></div><div class="crayon-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5a850741294-7"><span class="crayon-sy">)</span></div></div></td>
					</tr>
				</table>
			</div>
		</div>
<!-- [Format Time: 0.0001 seconds] -->
<p>Because no <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">staging_bucket</span> is specified, the SDK constructs the default name, finds that the bucket exists (which the attacker prepared in Phase 1) and uploads the model artifacts to the existing bucket’s location – the attacker’s project.</p>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_xfovngyywd82"></a>Phase 4: The Replacement</h3>
<p>As a result of the victim's upload, the Cloud Storage <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">finalize</span> event triggers the attacker's Cloud Function, which immediately replaces the victim's legitimate model with the malicious payload. The entire swap occurs within the opportunity window, well before the P4SA reads the artifact. The service agent then reads the poisoned model instead of the original one, without the victim's knowledge.</p>
<p>The following timeline, captured from our proof of concept, illustrates the replacement flow:</p>
<p>T+0 ms Victim SDK uploads <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">model.joblib</span> (601 bytes)</p>
<p>T+804 ms Cloud Function detects new model</p>
<p>T+1,433 ms Cloud Function replaces new model with RCE payload (601→2,945 bytes)</p>
<p>T+2,460 ms P4SA reads the REPLACED model from the staging bucket</p>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_mftiukufpr17"></a>Phase 5: Victim Deploys the Model</h3>
<p>The victim deploys the model to an endpoint using standard SDK calls, as shown in the following code block:</p><!-- Crayon Syntax Highlighter v_2.7.2_beta -->

		<div id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5d156946766" class="crayon-syntax crayon-theme-classic crayon-font-monaco crayon-os-pc print-yes notranslate" data-settings=" minimize scroll-mouseover wrap" style=" margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 12px; font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important;">
		
			<div class="crayon-toolbar" data-settings=" mouseover overlay hide delay" style="font-size: 12px !important;height: 18px !important; line-height: 18px !important;"><span class="crayon-title"></span>

			<div class="crayon-info" style="min-height: 16.8px !important; line-height: 16.8px !important;"></div>
			<div class="crayon-plain-wrap"><textarea  class="crayon-plain print-no" data-settings="dblclick" readonly style="-moz-tab-size:4; -o-tab-size:4; -webkit-tab-size:4; tab-size:4; font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important;">
endpoint = aiplatform.Endpoint.create(display_name="my-endpoint")
vertex_model.deploy(endpoint=endpoint, machine_type="n1-standard-2",
                    min_replica_count=1, max_replica_count=1)</textarea></div>
			<div class="crayon-main" style="">
				<table class="crayon-table">
					<tr class="crayon-row">
				<td class="crayon-nums " data-settings="show">

				</td>
						<td class="crayon-code"><div class="crayon-pre" style="font-size: 12px !important; line-height: 15px !important; -moz-tab-size:4; -o-tab-size:4; -webkit-tab-size:4; tab-size:4;"><div class="crayon-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5d156946766-1"><span class="crayon-i">endpoint</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span>=<span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">aiplatform</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-i">Endpoint</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-e">create</span><span class="crayon-sy">(</span><span class="crayon-i">display_name</span>=<span class="crayon-s">"my-endpoint"</span><span class="crayon-sy">)</span></div><div class="crayon-line crayon-striped-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5d156946766-2"><span class="crayon-i">vertex_model</span><span class="crayon-sy">.</span><span class="crayon-e">deploy</span><span class="crayon-sy">(</span><span class="crayon-i">endpoint</span>=<span class="crayon-i">endpoint</span><span class="crayon-sy">,</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">machine_type</span>=<span class="crayon-s">"n1-standard-2"</span><span class="crayon-sy">,</span></div><div class="crayon-line" id="crayon-6a348c6f87d5d156946766-3"><span class="crayon-h">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</span><span class="crayon-i">min_replica_count</span>=<span class="crayon-cn">1</span><span class="crayon-sy">,</span><span class="crayon-h"> </span><span class="crayon-i">max_replica_count</span>=<span class="crayon-cn">1</span><span class="crayon-sy">)</span></div></div></td>
					</tr>
				</table>
			</div>
		</div>
<!-- [Format Time: 0.0001 seconds] -->
<p>The victim has no indication that the model artifacts were tampered with.</p>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_e1wuwdzchr8o"></a>Phase 6: Code Execution</h3>
<p>When the serving container starts, it calls <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">joblib.load()</span> to deserialize the model. The <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">__reduce__</span> method in the poisoned payload executes immediately, before the container performs any type validation on the loaded object. In our proof of concept, the payload:</p>
<ol>
<li>Queries the GCE metadata server for the service account email and OAuth access token</li>
<li>Collects container environment variables (such as project number, endpoint ID, Kubernetes metadata)</li>
<li>Exfiltrates the credentials to an attacker-controlled webhook</li>
</ol>
<p>Figure 2 shows the six phases of the attack chain.</p>
<figure id="attachment_182522" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-182522" style="width: 800px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-182522 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-657406-182510-2.png" alt="A diagram illustrating the attack phases of a cloud-based security breach. The phases include preparing a bucket, replacing a model, model upload, deploying the model, operating the model, and code execution. The process shows interactions between &quot;Attacker Project,&quot; &quot;User Project,&quot; and &quot;Tenant Project.&quot; Arrows indicate data flow, including model upload, replacement, and deployment actions leading to credential exfiltration." width="800" height="1167" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-657406-182510-2.png 972w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-657406-182510-2-302x440.png 302w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-657406-182510-2-480x700.png 480w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-657406-182510-2-768x1120.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 800px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-182522" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 2. Attack chain flow.</figcaption></figure>
<h2><a id="post-182510-_fu184eqmtpf8"></a>Token Exfiltration, Post-Exploitation and Impact</h2>
<p>The OAuth token that was exfiltrated to the attacker’s webhook belongs to a service account running in Google's managed tenant project, named <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">custom-online-prediction@&lt;tenant-project&gt;.iam.gserviceaccount[.]com</span>. This token has <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">cloud-platform</span> <a href="https://oauth.net/2/scope/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">scope</a> – the broadest possible scope in Google Cloud.</p>
<p>We found that this token allows access to several tenant project resources that extend well beyond the scope of the individual deployment:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Cross-deployment model theft</strong>: The service account can access GCS buckets belonging to other model deployments within the same tenant project. In our testing environment, we were able to discover and read model artifacts from other deployments, including a complete TensorFlow model with trained weights.</li>
<li><strong>BigQuery reconnaissance</strong>: The token can enumerate all BigQuery datasets and table names in the victim's project, and read dataset access control lists. This exposes data schema, naming conventions and the identities of other service accounts with data access. This is valuable information for lateral movement.</li>
<li><strong>Tenant infrastructure intelligence</strong>: The token can read Cloud Logging from the Google-managed tenant project, revealing internal infrastructure details like:
<ul>
<li>Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster names</li>
<li>Active prediction deployments from other workloads</li>
<li>Google-internal container image URIs</li>
<li>Kubernetes system identities</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h2><a id="post-182510-_2hqm5rjd6lyi"></a>Mitigation and Collaboration With Google</h2>
<p>We reported this vulnerability to the Google security team. Google deployed fixes in <a href="https://github.com/googleapis/python-aiplatform/compare/v1.143.0...v1.144.0" target="_blank" rel="noopener">v1.144.0</a> on March 31, 2026 and in <a href="https://github.com/googleapis/python-aiplatform/releases/tag/v1.148.0" target="_blank" rel="noopener">v1.148.0</a> on April 15, 2026.</p>
<p>Figure 3 shows the first fix: the addition of a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">uuid4</span> variable with a randomly generated value to the end of the bucket naming routine in the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;"><a href="https://github.com/googleapis/python-aiplatform/compare/v1.143.0...v1.144.0#diff-60a5ac9185a90497595a64bd4e5be560e4ab37c27f3963e1ec7cc1ed6895a797" target="_blank" rel="noopener">gcs_utils.py</a></span> script.</p>
<figure id="attachment_182533" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-182533" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-182533 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-659769-182510-3.png" alt="A screenshot of a code comparison between two versions of a Python file. It highlights changes related to the creation of a staging bucket. The left side shows the old version where a specific bucket name is generated using a joined string and location. The right side, the updated version, adds a variable to the bucket name. Changes are marked with red and green highlights to indicate deletions and additions, respectively. A red arrow points to the new line with the UUID function." width="1000" height="460" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-659769-182510-3.png 2048w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-659769-182510-3-786x362.png 786w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-659769-182510-3-1520x700.png 1520w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-659769-182510-3-768x354.png 768w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-659769-182510-3-1536x707.png 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-182533" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 3. Change log for the first fix. Source: GitHub.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Figure 4 shows the second fix: the addition of a <a href="https://github.com/googleapis/python-aiplatform/commit/9feda020a1fb0d967b122468c1dd49f09a6ba456#diff-60a5ac9185a90497595a64bd4e5be560e4ab37c27f3963e1ec7cc1ed6895a797" target="_blank" rel="noopener">bucket ownership verification check</a> to the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">gcs_utils.py</span> script.</p>
<figure id="attachment_182544" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-182544" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-182544 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-662917-182510-4.png" alt="A screenshot of a split view of a code file with differences highlighted in green and red. The left side displays the original code, and the right side shows modifications. A red arrow points to a line on the right side, indicating changes related to verifying bucket ownership in the Google Cloud platform utils script. " width="1000" height="501" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-662917-182510-4.png 2048w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-662917-182510-4-786x394.png 786w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-662917-182510-4-1397x700.png 1397w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-662917-182510-4-768x385.png 768w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/word-image-662917-182510-4-1536x770.png 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-182544" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 4. Change log for the second fix. Source: GitHub.</figcaption></figure>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_u1ak93dqmytf"></a><strong>Disclosure Timeline</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>March 5, 2026: Vulnerability reported to Google Cloud via the Vulnerability Reward Program</li>
<li>March 9, 2026: Google assigned top priority to the report</li>
<li>March 10, 2026: Google acknowledged the vulnerability, assigned top severity and reported to the product team</li>
<li>March 31, 2026: Google deployed the first fix to production</li>
<li>April 15, 2026: Google deployed the second fix to production</li>
</ul>
<h2><a id="post-182510-_2an8ryq91inv"></a>Conclusion</h2>
<p>The growing role of AI in production systems highlights the importance of continuously examining the security resilience of the platforms that support it. This research is one contribution to that effort, and we appreciate Google's collaboration in resolving the vulnerability.</p>
<p>Our research shows that cloud security extends into the developer toolchain and machine learning model lifecycle. The vulnerability that we discovered demonstrates how seemingly minor design flaws can lead to a critical security issue. In vulnerable versions of the SDK, this attack requires no access to the victim's project and no social engineering tactics, and could result in model poisoning, credential theft and cross-tenant compromise.</p>
<p>Google Cloud worked closely with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 to resolve this issue through our Vulnerability Rewards Program (VRP). They deployed a permanent fix for the Vertex AI SDK for Python in version 1.148.0 on April 15, 2026.</p>
<p>We recommend that all developers update their SDK to version 1.148.0 or later to ensure the new bucket ownership checks are active. As an added best practice, when specifying an <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">artifact_uri</span> that isn't set to a Cloud Storage (<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">gs://</span>) location, users should set the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">staging_bucket</span> parameter to a Cloud Storage location to help ensure full asset isolation.</p>
<h3><a id="post-182510-_lsbythhc3nz9"></a><strong>Palo Alto Networks Protection and Mitigation</strong></h3>
<p>Palo Alto Networks customers are better protected from the threats discussed above through the following products:</p>
<p><strong>Cortex Cloud</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Organizations are better equipped to<a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/apps/pan/public/downloadResource?pagePath=/content/pan/en_US/resources/whitepapers/close-ai-security-gap" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> close the AI security gap</a> through the deployment of <a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/cortex/cloud/ai-security-posture-management" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Cortex AI-SPM</a>, which delivers comprehensive visibility and posture management for AI agents across AWS, Azure and GCP environments, as described within this article. Cortex AI-SPM is designed to mitigate critical risks including, over-privileged AI agent access, misconfigurations, and unauthorized data exposure. Cortex AI-SPM enables security teams to enforce compliance with NIST and OWASP standards, monitor for real-time behavioral anomalies, and secure the entire AI lifecycle within a unified cloud security context.</li>
<li>Cortex Cloud <a href="https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/r/Cortex-CLOUD/Cortex-Cloud-Runtime-Security-Documentation/What-is-Cortex-Cloud-Identity-Security" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Identity Security</a> can also protect organizations from the techniques discussed in the article. Identity Security encompasses:
<ul>
<li>Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM)</li>
<li>Identity Security Posture Management (ISPM)</li>
<li>Data Access Governance (DAG)</li>
<li>Identity Threat Detection and Response (ITDR)</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>

<script>
 var PAN_LOAD_RECAPTCHA_LANGUAGE = 'en_US';

(function($) {
	// Migrated from the unit42-v5 + Modifications
	var subscribeSuccess = false;
	var email = document.getElementById('newsletter-email');
	var subscription_form = document.getElementById('unit42footerSubscription_form');
	var subscription_form_button = document.getElementById('unit42footerSubscription_form_button');
        var isCaptchaComplete02  = false;	
        window.captchaInlineFormOnload = function(token){
            isCaptchaComplete02 = true;
            $("form[name='Unit42_Subscribe'] button[id='unit42footerSubscription_form_button']").prop('disabled', false);
        }
        var PAN_INLINE_FORM_RECAPTCHA_LOADED = false;
        const SITE_KEY = '6LdDKhIsAAAAABdoYV3PR5VJ2Gz23_dLSvq2uvBQ'; 
                if(!PAN_INLINE_FORM_RECAPTCHA_LOADED){
               PAN_INLINE_FORM_RECAPTCHA_LOADED = true;
               // trigger loading api.js (recaptcha.js) script
               var recapthaScript = $("script[src='https://www.google.com/recaptcha/enterprise.js?render="+SITE_KEY+"&hl="+PAN_LOAD_RECAPTCHA_LANGUAGE+"&onload=captchaInlineFormOnload']").length
               // console.log("recapthaScript",recapthaScript);
               if (!recapthaScript) {
                   var head = document.getElementsByTagName('head')[0];
                   var script = document.createElement('script');
                   script.typerecapthaScript = 'text/javascript';
                   script.src = "https://www.google.com/recaptcha/enterprise.js?render="+SITE_KEY+"&hl="+PAN_LOAD_RECAPTCHA_LANGUAGE+"&onload=captchaInlineFormOnload";
                   head.appendChild(script);
               }
               else{
                   captchaInlineFormOnload();
                }
           }
            	
	
	$(subscription_form).submit(function(e) {
		e.preventDefault();
		e.stopImmediatePropagation();
		updateEmailMask();
		var success = true;
		var form = $(this);
		var mail = form.find('input[name="Email"]');
		
		if (mail.val() === '') {
			mail.addClass('has-error');
			showError(1);
			success = false;	
		}  else if (!isEmail(mail.val())){
			showError(2);
			success = false;
		}
		else {
			mail.removeClass('has-error');
			$('.error-mail').addClass('d-none');
		}

		

		if (success) {
                                                if(grecaptcha){
                        grecaptcha.enterprise.ready(function() {
                            grecaptcha.enterprise.execute(SITE_KEY, {action: 'submit'}).then(function(token) {
                                submitSubscribeForm({token :token, action : 'submit'},form);
                            });
                        });
                    }
                    			
		}
		return false;
	});
        function submitSubscribeForm(tokenData, form){
            var serialized_data = form.serialize();
            let captchaParams = `&g-recaptcha-response=${tokenData.token}&action=${tokenData.action}`;
            $.ajax({
				type: 'POST',
				url: form.attr('action'),
				data: serialized_data+captchaParams,
				beforeSend: function() {
                 form.find('button').addClass('is-loading');
    			},
				success: function(msg) {
					form.find('.form-success-message').html('<p class="success-message">You have been successfully subscribed</p>');
					form.find('button').removeClass('is-loading');
					$(email).val('');
					clearError();
				},
				error: function(jqXHR, textStatus, errorThrown) {
					$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled', true);
					form.find('button').removeClass('is-loading');
					
				}
			});
            
        }
	function showError(error_type){
		if(error_type == 1) {
			$('.error-mail').text("Please enter the email address.").addClass('error-show');
			$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled');
		} else if(error_type == 2){
			$('.error-mail').text("Please provide a valid e-mail address.").addClass('error-show');
			$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled');
		}	
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-loading');
	}
	function clearError(){
		$('.error-mail').text("").removeClass('error-show');;
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-loading');
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-disabled');
	}
	
	$(email).on('input', function (event) { 
		var email = $(this).val();
		if (isEmail(email) ) {			
			clearError();
		} else if(email == ""){
			clearError();
		} else{
			showError(2);			  
		}
    });

	function isEmail(email) {
		var re = /^(([^<>()\[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+(\.[^<>()\[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+)*)|(".+"))@((\[[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\])|(([a-zA-Z\-0-9]+\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}))$/;
		return re.test(String(email).toLowerCase());
	}
	
	
	
	function updateEmailMask() {
		var email = $("#unit42footerSubscription_form input[name='Email']").val();
		if (email && email.trim() != '') {
			var maskedEmail = maskEmailAddress(email);
			$("#unit42footerSubscription_form input[name='emailFormMask']").val(maskedEmail);
		}
	}

	function maskEmailAddress (emailAddress) {
		function mask(str) {
			var strLen = str.length;
			if (strLen > 4) {
				return str.substr(0, 1) + str.substr(1, strLen - 1).replace(/\w/g, '*') + str.substr(-1,1);
			}
			return str.replace(/\w/g, '*');
		}
		return emailAddress.replace(/([\w.]+)@([\w.]+)(\.[\w.]+)/g, function (m, p1, p2, p3) {
			return mask(p1) + '@' + mask(p2) + p3;
		});

		return emailAddress;
	}

}(jQuery));
//# sourceMappingURL=main.js.map
	
</script>

<script type="text/javascript">
	$(document).ready(function(){
		$("html").on("click", ".language-btn", function () {
			$(this).toggleClass("expand");
			$(".language-dropdown").toggleClass("expand");
		});

		$("html").on("click", "body", function (b) {
			if (!$(b.target).is(".language-btn")) {
				$(".language-btn").removeClass("expand");
				$(".language-dropdown").removeClass("expand");
			}
		});
	});
</script>

	var isProcessing = false; 
    function alter_ul_post_values(obj,post_id,ul_type){
	
		if (isProcessing)    
		return;  
		isProcessing = true;   
		var like_nonce = jQuery('#_wpnonce').val();
		jQuery(obj).find("span").html("..");
                jQuery.ajax({
                    type: "POST",
                    url: "https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/plugins/like-dislike-counter-for-posts-pages-and-comments/ajax_counter.php",
                    data: "post_id="+post_id+"&up_type="+ul_type+"&ul_nonce="+like_nonce,
                    success: function(msg){
                            jQuery(obj).find("span").html(msg);
                            isProcessing = false; 
                            jQuery(obj).find('svg').children('path').attr('stroke','#0050FF');
                            jQuery(obj).removeClass('idc_ul_cont_not_liked idc_ul_cont_not_liked_inner');
                    }
 		});
	}
	</script>

function noSell(event) {
    event.preventDefault();
   if (( typeof OneTrust != 'undefined') &&  (!!OneTrust)) {
       OneTrust.ToggleInfoDisplay();
    }else{
      var href = event.target.getAttribute('href');
        window.open(href, '_blank'); 
    }
}

function loadScript(url, defer){
    var script1 = document.createElement('script');
    script1.setAttribute('type', 'text/javascript');
    script1.setAttribute('src',url);
    if(defer == true){
        script1.setAttribute('defer','defer');
    }
    document.head.appendChild(script1);
}
function loadScript1(url, callback){

    var script = document.createElement("script")
    script.type = "text/javascript";
    if (script.readyState){  //IE
        script.onreadystatechange = function(){
            if (script.readyState == "loaded" || script.readyState == "complete"){
                script.onreadystatechange = null;
                callback();
            }
        };
    } else {  //Others
        script.onload = function(){
            callback();
        };
    }
    script.src = url;
    document.getElementsByTagName("head")[0].appendChild(script);
}
if(referer == "CloudCortex" || referer == "Prisma" || referer == "Cortex" || referer == "Sase" || referer == "Unit" || referer == "Ngfw" || referer == "Idira"){

    setTimeout(function(){
      loadScript(main_site_criticalTopBase, false);
      loadScript1(main_site_criticalTopProductNav, function(){
        window.PAN_initializeProduct2021Nav();
      });
      loadScript(main_site_defered, false);
    }, 3000);

      loadScript1(main_site_critical_top, function(){
        window.PAN_initializeProduct2021Nav();
      });
      loadScript(main_site_defered, false);
    }, 3000);
	}
}

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {
  // Find all the forms on the page
  var forms = document.getElementsByTagName("form");

  // Loop through each form
  for (var i = 0; i < forms.length; i++) {
    var form = forms[i];

    // Check if the hidden input field already exists
    var requestInput = form.querySelector("input[name='web_unit42_req_id']");
    if (!requestInput) {
      // Create a hidden input element if it doesn't exist
      requestInput = document.createElement("input");
      requestInput.type = "hidden";
      requestInput.name = "web_unit42_req_id";
      requestInput.id = "web_unit42_req_id";

      // Append the hidden field to the form
      form.appendChild(requestInput);
    }
  }
});

// Assign the onCheqResponse function to the window object to handle events from any form
window.onCheqResponse = function(encryptedMessage, requestID) {
  // Find all the forms on the page
  var forms = document.getElementsByTagName("form");

  for (var i = 0; i < forms.length; i++) {
    var form = forms[i];
    var requestInput = form.querySelector("input[name='web_unit42_req_id']");
    if (requestInput) {
      requestInput.value = requestID;
    }
  }
};
